extracted.intended_audience: readers of a short-story annual; aspiring short-story writers and anthology editors
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial selection and presentation of short stories for a 'best of the year' anthology, with an introductory commentary on story-writing textbooks and contemporary contributions to the field. The page includes the editor's selection note and a representative short story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anthology arrangement and non-ranking disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Note. The twenty stories which follow are arranged in the alphabetical order of their authors' names. This arrangement does not imply any precedence in merit of particular stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor explicitly arranges selections alphabetically by author and states that this ordering should not be read as a ranking of merit. Use an ordering that avoids implying comparative precedence when presenting a curated selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor selection criterion — 'best' from American magazines
rubrics_metrics.description: It is my pleasure and honor this year to dedicate the best that I have found in the American magazines as the fruit of my labors to Wilbur Daniel Steele...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor's selection standard is based on personal judgment of what he considered the 'best' material appearing in American magazines during the year. Selections are curated from contemporary periodical publication and presented as representative excellence according to the editor's evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: What makes a definitive textbook on story writing
rubrics_metrics.description: In 'A Handbook on Story Writing,' Dr. Blanche Colton Williams has written the first definitive textbook on the subject. Its many predecessors have either been content to deal with narrow branches in the same field, or have exploited quite frankly and shamelessly the commercial possibilities of story writing as a cheap trade. Dr. Williams's book will not be in all likelihood superseded for many years to come, and the effects of her work are already to be seen in the short stories of many established writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'definitive' handbook is characterized here by comprehensive coverage of the subject (as opposed to dealing only with narrow branches) and by resisting purely commercial, 'cheap trade' exploitation. Longevity and demonstrable influence on contemporary practitioners are cited as marks of a superior guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary notability as 'permanent contribution'
rubrics_metrics.description: Thomas Burke, Caradoc Evans, and Arthur Machen have added permanent contributions to English literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor signals that works (or authors) considered notable are those adding 'permanent contributions' to the literature — i.e., works with lasting value and influence beyond ephemeral popularity. This is used as an evaluative standard when surveying a year's output.
